summary: The winner names the loser once, in a clause, with a nod to their service or a call that has been made.
realLife: Three winners name the loser by name once; one names only the loser's office; two never mention them. None attacks the loser.

inGame: filings and contests give the opponent's name and office; needs: a record that the loser called or was called on election night

turns.way: The winner never names the loser.
turns.pulledBy: a bitter race; the opponent was a rival of the winner's
turns.writes: no opponent in the speech; the loser notices at home

turns.way: The winner spends a paragraph on the loser, with praise.
turns.pulledBy: a loser who served long in town; a gracious, fair-minded winner
turns.writes: a longer thanks to the loser; the town hears it in the news
